originality.rationale: Full Zhao–Uchida Secs. 2 and 5 provide the general construction and transverse Jacobian but only sample an unstable triangular sector for M=8; the present M=3 all-active exact stable example and weak-to-strong reversal are not implied by that numerical sample. The near-incoherent full-amplitude theory of León–Pazó assumes identical local oscillators. Generalized-splay stability of Berner et al. treats phase networks rather than the exact six-real-dimensional heterogeneous Stuart–Landau Jacobian. Specific published-finding corpus and literature searches exposed no equivalent stability certificate, subject to residual historical-priority risk.

value.rationale: The smallest noncollinear polygon is a triangle. A fully active, genuinely heterogeneous three-node zero-mean phase-locked state with exact strict full-amplitude stability resolves an essential feasibility boundary suggested but not settled by the 2026 eight-node sample. Its coupling continuation rigorously changes transverse behavior from unstable near zero to stable at finite positive coupling. The exact algebraic certificate is interpretable and repeatable and supports further quantitative bifurcation analysis, while no global-basin or transition-location theorem is claimed.
